example: At today's 9 a.m. budget review in conference room B, my manager rolled his eyes right after I asked for the spreadsheet update.
My teenager muttered "whatever" and slammed the bedroom door after I asked about homework tonight.
At dinner tonight at Sam's Diner, a friend said "You're too sensitive" when I declined the joke.
During Tuesday's 2 p.m. planning stand-up, my colleague whispered to Taylor and they both laughed right after I described the roadmap change.
Yesterday evening in the kitchen, my partner said "You never listen" when we talked about chores.
During this morning's 10 a.m. project video call, the client's audio overlapped mine three times when I proposed a change.
A coworker slammed her notebook shut and walked out during my presentation yesterday.
During last night's game, the referee missed three fouls against our team.
The barista skipped me and served two people who arrived later in line this afternoon.
At the grocery store, another shopper reached over me to grab the last carton of eggs.
My roommate left dirty dishes piled in the sink again before leaving for work.
My sibling borrowed my car without asking and returned it with the tank empty.
The email from HR said my contract wasn't renewed with no explanation.
The teacher handed back my child's assignment with "sloppy" written across the top.
I received a performance review that only listed mistakes without any concrete examples.
The landlord hasn't responded to three messages about the leak this week.
The contractor missed today's 8 a.m. appointment and hasn't texted or called.
My doctor glanced at the clock twice while I was describing my symptoms today.
In last Thursday's sprint retrospective, the project lead assigned me every follow-up action item again.
My boss sent me three Slack messages between 11 p.m. and midnight about tomorrow's report.
My partner scrolled through their phone during dinner instead of looking up.
The rideshare driver talked loudly on speakerphone for the entire trip yesterday.
My neighbor's dog barked loudly for 30 minutes starting at 6 a.m. on Saturday.
A cyclist sped through the crosswalk even though the light was red this morning.
I caught myself scrolling for an hour instead of calling my grandmother back.
My coworker double-checked the expense report and caught a mistake before we sent it.
At the 8 a.m. session, the gym trainer high-fived me right after I racked 185 pounds on squats.
My neighbor shoveled our sidewalk after the snowstorm while we were at work.
At 4 p.m., the coordinator emailed me listing the volunteer shifts I covered during the fundraiser.
During therapy, my counselor paused and reflected back exactly what I said before offering input.
My partner cooked dinner and cleaned the kitchen while I finished my deadline.
During Monday's sprint review, the project manager assigned two follow-up tasks to each teammate.
Outside the market at 3 p.m., a stranger handed back my wallet with the cash still inside the billfold.
My boss approved my vacation request the same day I submitted it.
The nurse checked in twice during the night to make sure my dad was comfortable.
My dentist explained each step before starting the procedure.
At 7 p.m. the delivery app marked my order as delivered while the porch camera still showed an empty doorstep.
My friend arrived 30 minutes late to lunch without texting.
Our HOA sent a warning letter about lawn length without asking first.
My colleague took credit for my idea during the pitch meeting.
The daycare forgot to call when my child had a fever.
The bus driver waited for me when I was running toward the stop.
From Monday through Friday, no cards under my teammate's initials moved on the shared sprint board.
Our landlord repaired the leaky faucet the day after we reported it.
My sibling promised to pay me back Friday but still hasn't sent anything.
The restaurant served my meal with peanuts after I noted my allergy.
My manager scheduled a meeting over my lunch break without asking.
Yesterday the service agent stayed on the call for each troubleshooting step and emailed this morning to confirm the fix.
The city finally fixed the streetlight after months of emails.
